title: Aging‐Induced Ductile‐Brittle‐Ductile Transition in High‐Entropy Alloys and its Implications

recollection.starting_material: High-entropy alloys (likely a CoCrFeMnNi or similar equiatomic system)
recollection.intervention: Thermal aging at elevated temperatures for varying durations
recollection.structure: Aging-induced precipitation of secondary phases (e.g., sigma phase or Laves phase) leading to a microstructural evolution from a single-phase FCC to a multiphase composite
recollection.mechanism: Precipitation hardening initially increases strength but reduces ductility (brittle transition), followed by a recovery of ductility due to strain localization or phase transformation at longer aging times (ductile-brittle-ductile transition)
recollection.results: A non-monotonic change in fracture toughness and elongation with aging time, where ductility first drops significantly then recovers, with a peak in yield strength occurring at intermediate aging times.

score.note: The recollection only generically identifies thermal aging, which is already implied by the title, and gives no correct temperatures. It misidentifies the alloy and microstructural evolution: the actual material is as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC+B2 phases, and the key mediator is enhanced L12 ordering plus jagged B2/FCC boundaries, not sigma/Laves precipitation from single-phase FCC. The proposed precipitation-hardening mechanism does not capture the actual APBE/modulus, planar-slip, boundary stress-concentration, reduced-ordering, and ductile-transition-zone mechanisms. No numerical results are provided.
